summary: A compact token — a filter you toggle, a suggestion you take, or a value you remove.

pairs.dont: Signal that a chip is selected with the fill alone.
pairs.do: Leave the check on — it is what carries selection.
pairs.why: On hover, focus and press a selected chip takes the same fill as an unselected one. Remove the check and three of the five states stop telling you anything.

pairs.dont: Set `selected` on a chip that performs an action.
pairs.do: Use `selected` only for something that stays on; leave it off for a one-shot.
pairs.why: `aria-pressed` promises a state that persists. On a chip that just runs a search, it announces a toggle that does not exist.

pairs.dont: Make a removable token clickable as a whole as well.
pairs.do: Let the ✕ be the only control on it.
pairs.why: A button inside a button is invalid HTML, and a token with two overlapping hit areas is a coin toss for anyone using a pointer imprecisely.

pairs.dont: Ship a row of tokens whose controls are all called "Remove".
pairs.why: A screen reader lists controls out of context. Twelve identical "Remove" buttons is twelve coin tosses.

pairs.dont: Reach for a chip because it is a smaller, rounder button.
pairs.do: Use chips for values — filters, tokens, suggestions. Use a Button for a command.
pairs.why: Chips read as things you are collecting or narrowing by. A verb in a pill just looks like a button that lost an argument with the grid.

pairs.dont: Recolour a chip to carry status.
pairs.do: Use a Badge when the point is what something is, not what you are filtering by.
pairs.why: Chip is deliberately one neutral ramp. Status lives in Badge, which has the tones and the semantics for it.

a11y: A selectable chip sets aria-pressed — it is a toggle button, not a checkbox, so it announces "pressed" rather than "checked".
The remove button is a separate control with removeLabel as its aria-label: reachable by keyboard without activating the chip itself.
Disabled sets pointer-events-none on the chip and on its remove button, so neither is clickable while both stay readable.
